'''Herman Chernoff''' (July 1, 1923 – July 6, 2026) was an American [[applied mathematics|applied mathematician]], [[statistician]] and physicist. He was a professor at [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]], [[Stanford University|Stanford]], [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]], and at [[Harvard University]].<ref>
{{cite journal
 |last1       = Bather
 |first1      = John
 |journal     = [[Statistical Science]]
 |title       = A conversation with Herman Chernoff
 |volume      = 11
 |issue       = 4
 |pages       = 335–350
 |year        = 1996
 |doi         = 10.1214/ss/1032280306
 |doi-access= free
 }}
</ref>{{r|mactutor}}

==Early life and education==
Herman Chernoff's parents were Pauline and Max Chernoff, Jewish immigrants from the [[Russian Empire]]. He studied at [[Townsend Harris High School]]<ref name=mactutor>{{cite web|title=Herman Chernoff|publisher=[[MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive]]|url=http://www-groups.dcs.st-and.ac.uk/history/Biographies/Chernoff.html|access-date=12 March 2020}}</ref> and earned a [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] in [[mathematics]] from the [[City College of New York]] in 1943.<ref name=mit>{{cite web|title=Herman Chernoff|work=Faculty directory|publisher=[[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]]|url=http://math.mit.edu/directory/profile.php?pid=43|access-date=12 March 2020|archive-date=7 October 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221007023911/https://math.mit.edu/directory/profile.php?pid=43|url-status=dead}}</ref> He attended graduate school at [[Brown University]], earning an [[Master of Science|M.Sc.]] in [[applied mathematics]] in 1945, and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in applied mathematics in 1948 under the supervision of [[Abraham Wald]].{{r|mit}}<ref name=mathgen>{{cite web|title=Herman Chernoff|publisher=[[Mathematics Genealogy Project]]|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/index.php|access-date=12 March 2020}}</ref>

==Recognition==
Chernoff became a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1974,<ref>{{cite web|title=Herman Chernoff|work=Member Directory|date=September 2024 |publisher=[[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]|url=https://www.amacad.org/person/herman-chernoff}}</ref> and was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 1980.<ref>{{cite web|title=Herman Chernoff|work=Member directory|publisher=[[National Academy of Sciences]]|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/herman-chernoff-slgqsg/}}</ref> In 1987, he was selected for the [[Wilks Memorial Award]] by the American Statistical Association,<ref>{{cite web|title=Samuel S Wilks Award of the American Statistical Association|publisher=[[MacTutor History of Mathematics archive]]|url=http://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Honours/Wilks_award.html}}</ref> and in 2012, he was made an inaugural fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2012-11-10</ref>

==Personal life and death==
Chernoff met his future wife, Judith, when they were both graduate students at Brown University in 1945, and married her in 1947.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Siliezar |first1=Juan |title=A sense of humor, giving space, trying to listen: Advice from 73 years of marriage |url=https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2021/04/after-73-years-of-marriage-their-advice-remains-the-same/ |website=The Harvard Gazette |access-date=25 September 2024}}</ref> She died at the age of 98 on June 9, 2023.<ref>{{cite web |title=Judith Chernoff |url=https://www.dignitymemorial.com/obituaries/brookline-ma/judith-chernoff-11327954 |website=Dignity Memorial |access-date=25 September 2024}}</ref> At the time of her death they were believed to be the oldest couple living in Massachusetts.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Stephanos |first1=Maria |title=Meet husband, wife believed to be oldest living couple in Massachusetts |url=https://www.wcvb.com/article/meet-husband-wife-believed-to-be-oldest-living-couple-in-massachusetts/35857262 |access-date=25 September 2024 |agency=WCVB-TV |date=Mar 16, 2021}}</ref>

Chernoff [[Centenarian|turned 100]] on July 1, 2023,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fortnow |first=Lance |title=Chernoff Turns 100 |url=https://blog.computationalcomplexity.org/2023/07/chernoff-turns-100.html |access-date=2023-07-02 |language=en}}</ref> and died in [[Boston]], Massachusetts, on July 6, 2026, at the age of 103.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Herman Chernoff |url=https://www.dignitymemorial.com/obituaries/brookline-ma/herman-chernoff-12959864 |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=Dignity Memorial |language=en-us}}</ref>
